summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver transplant was admitted with fever and worsening right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for infection in the setting of immunosuppression. Blood cultures and imaging showed no evidence of bacterial infection or biliary complications. The fever resolved, and she remained asymptomatic off antibiotics. Her symptoms were determined to be non-infectious, possibly related to underlying inflammation. She improved clinically, with stable lab values and liver function, and was discharged home on her baseline immunosuppressive regimen with instructions to follow up as scheduled.
